Subject: ACME call recap & next steps (RAG eval)

Hi Tom / Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side based on what we heard on the discovery:  

- Goal: Improve support search accuracy and reduce hallucinations for policy/FAQ content when surfaced in product UI.
- Current infra: ElasticSearch + basic BM25, occasional embeddings for re-rank; index size ~120k docs; average query length ~10-20 tokens.
- Top concern: Grounding metrics (precision@k, hallucination rate), and minimizing latency bump for end-users.

Proposed immediate work:  
1) Lightweight RAG eval run against your sample queries we discussed. We'll run 2 retrieval configs (dense faiss vs hybrid BM25+dense) and 2 reranker options (cross-encoder reranker vs dot-product reranker).
2) Model recommendations: start with a smaller generation baseline for safety (Redwood-7B-q4) and a higher-quality variant (Open-Avalanche-70B-pt-8bit) for headroom. We'll include calibrated temperature/stop sequences and suggested prompt templates.
3) Deliverables: evaluation report (precision@k, grounding score, latency), prompt set (30 canonical queries + edge cases), and recommended config for pilot.

Next steps I propose:
- We'll run a 48-72 hour eval on your sample set and share results.
- Schedule 30-min follow-up to review results and pick the pilot config (do you have availability Tue/Wed next week?).

Attachments: placeholder for prompt set and initial benchmark plan (I will send the full report once the run completes).

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Hey Marissa — thanks for the recap — this aligns. A couple quick clarifications before you kick off:  

1) Sample set: we can give you the 500-query export from Support Analytics (I'll share a link). Can you confirm the format you'd prefer? JSONL where each record is {query, doc_id, expected_answer}?
2) Latency constraint: our SLA target is P95 < 350ms added tail for RAG (including reranker). If cross-encoder reranker adds >200ms we probably need to consider batching or async rerank.
3) Can you include a small evaluation of grounding vs hallucination rate (we define hallucination as content returned that doesn't match any indexed doc and is asserted as fact)?

If you can confirm sample format and timeline, we'll get procurement looped in for any data transfer/NDAs.

Tom
Director, Product - ACME Corp

Hi team - small technical notes from our side as we prepare the run:  

1) Embedding model: for this workload I recommend redwood/sim-embed-2-small for index build (balance speed + accuracy). We'll do a quick sensitivity check vs sim-embed-2-large during the run.
2) Reranker tuning: if we use a cross-encoder, we'll test two distillation sizes - full cross-encoder for offline rerank (best accuracy) and a distilled cross-encoder that can run with lower latency (approx +40-60ms vs dot-product).
3) Grounding metric proposal (we'll include these in the report):
   - Precision@1, Precision@3
   - Grounding recall: fraction of answers where generated text cites at least one matching indexed doc passage (fuzzy match)
   - Hallucination rate: fraction of answers with >2 unsupported assertions (manual sampling + automated fuzzy-check)
   - Latency P50/P95 including reranker contribution

4) For the hybrid config: we'll start with BM25 (top 200) then dense re-rank (top 100) - this gives a good recall balance. We can lower numbers if latency is a problem.

I'll instrument the run to emit per-query traces and sample examples to make triage easier. Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the metrics.

- Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
